Session 3 Facilitator Rehearsal Run Sheet

Turn evidence into an opinionated choice

Version: 2026-08-23 Format: 135-minute live cohort session Cohort: up to 10 PMs with approximately 2-6 years of experience Deck: 19-page HTML/PDF facilitator deck Preparation: the Session 3 pre-read is not released in the current site build; do not treat the live deck as its substitute

This is a rehearsal document, not a teleprompter. It is intentionally fuller than the spoken delivery. Rehearse the argument, case logic, questions, transitions, and recovery language; then teach in your own voice.

The facilitator's job

By the end of the session, learners should be able to make an opinionated product choice without confusing:

  1. strategy with a goal, narrative, or collection of initiatives;
  2. coherence with completeness or certainty;
  3. portfolio lenses or prioritization scores with decision authority;
  4. sequence with a dated list; and
  5. cheaper code generation with cheaper product ownership.

The governing message is:

Strategy is an accountable interpretation of evidence that constrains allocation. It becomes operational through exclusions, sequence, thresholds, and ownership.

Session 2 ended with a calibrated belief, not a strategy. Evidence can narrow the credible interpretations, but it cannot mechanically choose the direction, allocate capacity, or own the lifecycle consequence. Those are Session 3 decisions.

Source and accuracy stance

  • The required teaching spine is Reforge-derived and reorganized into the course's own evidence-to-direction-to-portfolio-to-lifecycle chain.
  • The Noted product is real; Week 3 alternatives, constraints, estimates, candidates, and allocation are constructed for practice.WN-03
  • The PMF narrative material is used as a linked hypothesis system, not as a canvas-completion exercise.S3-SN-02
  • The portfolio categories widen consideration of different forms of product value. The course does not imply a universal allocation or fixed quota.S3-SN-05
  • AI coding agents are contemporary context for the technical-strategy decision. Current evidence is heterogeneous and context-dependent, so the session avoids universal productivity claims.S3-SN-12S3-SN-13
  • Learners are assessed on technical product judgment. Prompting, code generation, repository inspection, and shipping are deliberately outside the required capability.

Before learners arrive

  • Open the HTML deck and verify arrow-key navigation and fullscreen mode.
  • Keep a visible six-minute timer ready for slides 8, 13, and 17.
  • Prepare one capture surface with six headings: diagnosis, winning mechanism, exclusion, displaced opportunity, threshold, and owner.
  • Keep the Week 2 belief update visible. Do not reopen evidence-method selection unless a claim in the strategy exceeds its evidence.
  • Ask learners to make each decision individually. Select two or three answers yourself after time; there is no peer-discussion requirement.
  • Do not reveal the model direction or portfolio before individual work.
  • Treat every Week 3 option, estimate, percentage, and constraint as constructed.WN-03

Facilitation stance

Use five moves throughout:

  1. Name the diagnosis. Ask: "What is happening that makes this direction more coherent?"
  2. Trace the system. Ask: "Which linked hypothesis breaks if this assumption is false?"
  3. Make the exclusion costly. Ask: "What attractive opportunity are you actually declining?"
  4. Expose displacement. Ask: "If this is funded, what cannot be funded now?"
  5. Follow lifecycle ownership. Ask: "Who reviews, integrates, operates, and pays for this after the prototype works?"

Useful recovery phrases:

  • "That is a goal. What diagnosis explains the situation?"
  • "That is a list of six claims. Show me the causal or economic link between them."
  • "If the strategy cannot reject anything attractive, it is not constraining the portfolio."
  • "Use the score to inspect assumptions. Now make the call yourself."
  • "A fast prototype is evidence of producibility, not proof of product value or operability."
  • "Where did the constraint move after generation became cheaper?"
  • "Who owns the system in month six?"

Avoid these phrases:

  • "The data tells us which strategy to choose."
  • "We should pursue both and see what happens."
  • "Every work type deserves a balanced allocation."
  • "The highest RICE score wins."
  • "AI makes engineering effectively free."
  • "Build is now always better than buy."
  • "Tech debt" without naming its product, capacity, reliability, risk, or economic consequence.

Slide-by-slide rehearsal script

Slide 1 - Turn evidence into an opinionated choice

Time: 4 minutes Job: Reframe strategy as accountable choice after evidence, not the next planning artifact.

Rehearse

"Session 2 did not give us certainty. It gave us a belief that is calibrated enough to make a better choice. Today we convert that belief into direction, allocation, and a technical commitment."
"The recurring PM failure here is to move from evidence into a roadmap without making the strategy explicit. The roadmap looks decisive, but nobody can explain why one initiative reinforces how the product wins and another does not."
"We will choose a direction, make its portfolio consequences visible, and then recalculate one technical choice now that coding agents can make plausible software faster. The product decision still includes everything that happens after the code appears."

Ask

"Where does strategy live in your company today: in a shared choice, or mostly in presentation language and roadmap labels?"

Do not collect a round. Let learners locate the gap privately.

Transition

"We are building one choice record across three layers."

Slide 2 - One cumulative choice architecture

Time: 6 minutes Job: Show how direction, allocation, and technical calculus constrain one another.

Rehearse

"First, choose strategic direction. Diagnose the constraint and link audience, problem, value, advantage, growth, and economics into one revisable system."
"Second, allocate the portfolio. A direction becomes real only when it changes what receives capacity, what is sequenced first, and what waits."
"Third, inspect the technical choice inside that portfolio. Lower generation cost can change build, buy, adapt, and scope assumptions, but integration, review, risk, economics, maintenance, and operational ownership still follow the product."
"The Week 3 output is not a strategy deck. It is a Strategy and Constraint Choice: one record another PM, designer, or engineer can use to make a consistent local decision."

Listen for

If learners treat the layers as sequential documents, clarify:

"The layers are coupled. A technical consequence may force the portfolio to change; a portfolio constraint may force the direction to narrow. Coherence is the test across the whole record."

Transition

"Here is the strategic choice Noted now faces."

Slide 3 - Two credible Noted directions

Time: 6 minutes Job: Present a real trade-off without making the preferred option obvious or risk-free.

Rehearse

"Direction A is workflow depth: own reliable decision handoff for recurring enterprise meetings. It narrows the audience and deepens workflow, administration, and governance."
"Direction B is horizontal breadth: become a general AI meeting memory for individual knowledge workers. It promises faster self-serve reach and broader use cases, but the connection to the ownership-handoff mechanism is weaker."
"Both options can create value. The team has two engineers and one designer for eight weeks. Enterprise security review consumes two weeks. The weakest link in Direction A is repeatable admin-led distribution."
"The decision is not which idea sounds exciting. It is which direction should govern the cycle and what Noted must explicitly not pursue."

Ask

"What evidence from Session 2 favors each option? What still has to be interpreted rather than read directly from the evidence?"

Take two answers. Do not decide yet.

Transition

"The first act of strategy is to explain the situation."

Slide 4 - Diagnosis before direction

Time: 5 minutes Job: Separate diagnosis from goals, evidence lists, and solution preference.

Rehearse

"Reforge defines product strategy around how a product will win and warns that surface-level strategy understanding can produce locally attractive work that conflicts with the deeper mechanism.S3-SN-01 Our adaptation begins with a diagnosis because the direction needs an explanation of the situation it is responding to."
"The evidence says ownership handoff is plausible in a bounded context. The tension is whether Noted should add broader summary intelligence or make a narrower workflow reliable. The working diagnosis is that the constraint is not note creation; it is trusted handoff after consequential meetings."
"That diagnosis is still judgment. Another responsible PM could interpret the evidence differently. The standard is whether the interpretation respects the evidence, explains the tension, and supports a coherent choice."

Misconception recovery

If a learner gives a target:

"Two enterprise design partners is a goal. What condition or mechanism makes that goal hard and makes one response more coherent?"

Transition

"A diagnosis chooses the center of gravity. The next test is whether all the necessary hypotheses reinforce it."

Slide 5 - Linked strategic hypothesis system

Time: 5 minutes Job: Teach the PMF narrative as an interdependent decision system.

Rehearse

"Reforge's PMF narrative links six hypotheses: problem, target audience, value proposition, competitive advantage, growth strategy, and business model. It is dynamic because learning in one dimension should update the others.S3-SN-02"

Walk left to right. Keep the verbs explicit:

"Enterprise team leads experience implicit ownership. A trusted record turns meeting meaning into accountable handoff. Noted's potential advantage is context carried across transcript, decision, owner, and workspace. Growth may come through admin-led templates. Team-plan willingness must support the service and governance cost."
"The weakest link is growth. If admins do not adopt or spread the workflow, user value can be real while the strategic system remains commercially weak. A list of six plausible statements is not enough; the links carry the strategy."

Ask

"Which link, if false, would most change the direction rather than merely improve its wording?"

Transition

"A coherent system also needs to say no and to say when it will change."

Slide 6 - Coherence, exclusions, and revision

Time: 4 minutes Job: Make strategic coherence observable through behavior.

Rehearse

"Coherence means choices reinforce the winning mechanism. It does not mean every strategic dimension is equally strong, everyone agrees, or uncertainty has disappeared."
"For Noted, recurring decision-heavy meetings, workspace context, and admin distribution reinforce trusted handoff. Personal summary polish and every-meeting expansion are excluded for now. The strategy is revisable if admin adoption stalls, governance blocks deployment, or handoff does not affect repeat use."
"A revision trigger should alter funding, sequence, audience, or capability—not merely refresh a narrative. The portable test is whether another team can use the direction to reject a locally attractive idea without asking the PM."

Misconception recovery

If a learner proposes no exclusions:

"Then the direction has not constrained scarce capacity. Name the attractive thing that becomes less important because this choice is true."

Transition

"Even a coherent hypothesis is not the same as product-market fit."

Slide 7 - Multi-signal fit boundary

Time: 4 minutes Job: Prevent a favorable signal from becoming permission to scale the whole strategy.

Rehearse

"Reforge's PMF measurement argument explicitly rejects using one metric such as NPS, a PMF survey, retention, or growth as the sole determinant of fit.S3-SN-03 The important idea here is multi-signal and segment-specific judgment."
"Noted has stronger evidence of problem intensity, mixed repeat use, a weak growth path, unknown economics, and a plausible advantage. The responsible posture is a concentrated hypothesis worth testing. It is not proof of fit or permission to scale."
"The radar is a qualitative diagnostic, not a score. It keeps a strong signal from compensating invisibly for a strategically fatal weakness."

Transition

"Now choose the direction before seeing the model answer."

Slide 8 - Unit 7 individual decision

Time: 14 minutes total: 6 decide, 8 debrief Job: Observe whether learners can make and bound a coherent strategic choice.

Set up the decision

"You have six minutes. Choose one governing direction. State the diagnosis, winning mechanism, weakest linked hypothesis, evidence that changed your view, explicit exclusion, and revision trigger. Do not combine both options into a compromise."

Keep answers private until time. Then select two contrasting responses.

Model debrief

"My current choice is workflow depth for recurring enterprise decision meetings. The diagnosis is that trusted ownership handoff—not note creation—is the consequential constraint. The linked mechanism is narrow audience, reliable handoff value, context advantage, admin distribution, and team economics."
"I exclude general personal summary optimization and sales intelligence this cycle. The weakest link is repeatable admin-led distribution. I would reverse or narrow the choice if admin adoption stalls across the two design partners, governance prevents real use, or explicit handoff does not improve repeat behavior."

What strong judgment sounds like

  • The diagnosis explains why the direction fits the evidence.
  • The winning mechanism links all material hypotheses.
  • The exclusion is attractive enough to carry opportunity cost.
  • The trigger would change a real choice.
  • Uncertainty is visible without dissolving commitment.

Weak-answer recovery

If a learner says "pursue both":

"Under the stated capacity, what receives less time, what is delayed, and which winning mechanism governs conflicts?"

Transition

"The direction is only real when it changes the portfolio."

Slide 9 - Portfolio of product-work types

Time: 5 minutes Job: Make multiple forms of product value legible without imposing equal buckets.

Rehearse

"Reforge argues that different kinds of product work require different toolkits. Feature, growth, PMF expansion, and scaling work should not be forced into one process or success model.S3-SN-05 Technical-strategy material similarly distinguishes product, scale, and risk work by the outcomes they create.S3-SN-09"
"For Noted, decision-and-owner capture is feature work. Admin templates test growth. Sales intelligence is expansion. Permission redesign is scale or enablement. Retention controls address risk. Meeting-type instrumentation enables evidence."
"The categories widen the candidate set and explain value. They do not guarantee every category funding. Equal balance can be as unstrategic as feature dominance."

Ask

"Which candidate would be easiest to dismiss as non-product work? What product consequence makes it legible?"

Transition

"Now translate the company priority into an area-level allocation."

Slide 10 - Strategy to allocation

Time: 5 minutes Job: Show that translation requires interpretation and explicit displacement.

Rehearse

"Reforge describes strategic priorities as top-down direction that product leaders translate into product work. Incorporating the words is not enough; the work must be informed by the priority and by the product area's context.S3-SN-06"
"The company wants two enterprise design partners. The illustrative allocation emphasizes the handoff feature, permission and governance, an admin distribution test, and instrumentation. The exact percentages are not capacity truth. They communicate relative emphasis."
"The decisive part is the displaced work: sales intelligence, personal summary polish, and full architecture modernization. Strategy has changed the portfolio because those attractive candidates now wait."

Misconception recovery

If a learner argues every stakeholder request should receive a small slice:

"What fragmentation cost does that create, and which hypothesis is no longer tested with enough force?"

Transition

"A scoring system can help inspect the candidates, but it cannot make this strategic trade-off."

Slide 11 - Scores expose assumptions

Time: 4 minutes Job: Preserve prioritization support while rejecting false decision authority.

Rehearse

"Reforge's critique of RICE is not that comparison is useless. The problem is false precision, gaming, and the appearance that arithmetic has replaced the strategic call.S3-SN-04"
"Summary polish wins the illustrative score because it has broad reach, assumed impact, and low effort. Permission redesign scores much lower. Yet permission may remove the binding constraint on the chosen enterprise direction."
"Use the score to ask where reach, impact, confidence, and effort came from. Then bring back strategic fit, dependency, option value, risk, and ownership. The PM still has to say: I choose this, despite the score, because this assumption governs the direction."

Ask

"Which input in the highest score is most likely to be numerically tidy and strategically misleading?"

Transition

"Allocation says what receives capacity. Sequence says how the team learns before it becomes trapped."

Slide 12 - Strategic sequence and option value

Time: 4 minutes Job: Make sequence a decision about learning, dependencies, and reversibility.

Rehearse

"Reforge's workplan material moves beyond short-term roadmap detail and asks leaders to sequence work across periods. Technical strategy adds the need to break problems into manageable work that delivers customer value while preserving the long-term portfolio.S3-SN-07S3-SN-11"
"Noted first instruments meeting type and tests the admin template manually. It then ships explicit handoff to two partners, adds the minimum permission controls, and only then decides whether to deepen, expand, or stop."
"This is not waterfall. The work overlaps, but each stage earns the next commitment. The sequence creates an option to build deeper platform capability later and avoids committing to enterprise architecture before the workflow earns it."

Transition

"Make the portfolio and sequence decision now."

Slide 13 - Unit 8 individual decision

Time: 14 minutes total: 6 decide, 8 debrief Job: Test whether learners can allocate constrained capacity and own the opportunity cost.

Set up the decision

"Fund a bounded mix. For each commitment, state the value contribution, dependency, learning logic, and owner. Then name the most painful displaced opportunity and explain why the roadmap score does not own your call."

Model debrief

"I fund four things: explicit handoff as the core feature; minimum permissions and retention as enterprise enablement and risk control; a manual admin distribution test; and meeting-type instrumentation."
"I sequence the cheapest growth and observability tests first, deliver the value-bearing handoff slice to two partners, and add only the controls required for responsible use. I defer sales intelligence even though it could score well because it expands the audience before the chosen mechanism is established."
"The displaced opportunity is broader self-serve reach. The score remains useful for challenging input assumptions, but strategy, dependency, and risk determine the actual call."

What strong judgment sounds like

  • Work types connect to different product consequences.
  • The mix is visibly constrained rather than universally balanced.
  • A real opportunity is displaced.
  • Sequence buys evidence or removes a dependency.
  • Owners and revision points are explicit.

Transition to break

"Take eight minutes. When we return, assume the team can generate a plausible implementation much faster than it could last year. We will test which parts of the decision actually changed."

Slide 14 - The production-cost curve moved

Time: 7 minutes Job: Establish a current, evidence-calibrated AI-era premise without turning it into a productivity claim.

Rehearse

"Coding agents can independently perform multi-step software tasks, and software development is a major use case in current agent interaction data.S3-SN-12 That changes option generation and can reduce the time needed to produce a plausible implementation in some contexts."
"But capability is not a universal productivity effect. METR randomized 246 real tasks among experienced maintainers working in mature repositories and found that early-2025 AI tools slowed the measured work in that setting.S3-SN-13 The study is a contextual result, not a universal law in the other direction."
"The safe product conclusion is that the production cost curve has moved unevenly. The bottleneck can shift toward defining the task, supplying context, evaluating output, integrating with the system, releasing responsibly, and operating what survives."
"Cheaper plausible code increases the number of options we can inspect. It can also increase option sprawl and hidden ownership. That is why the technical calculus becomes more important, not less."

Misconception recovery

If a learner asks for a universal speedup number:

"There is no defensible universal multiplier. Task shape, repository maturity, developer familiarity, tool, review burden, and quality standard change the result. Use scenario ranges in your own context."

Transition

"Now recalculate build and buy with the changed production input."

Slide 15 - Build, buy, adapt, defer, or no-build

Time: 6 minutes Job: Expand the binary and follow the full lifecycle.

Rehearse

"Reforge's build-or-buy model considers strategic value, available resources, cost, and vendor reliability. Strategic value is central because a capability can be unique without being a meaningful source of differentiation.S3-SN-10"
"AI makes an adapted option more attractive: Noted can use a model API while keeping workflow logic and context integration in-house. But time to prototype is only one column. Data obligations, integration, control, vendor reliability, unit economics, review, and ongoing ownership remain."
"Notice that no-build is a real option. A manual workflow can test whether explicit handoff changes behavior before any intelligent capability is operationalized. Defer is also a decision, not failure."

Ask

"Which option produces the fastest evidence about the product mechanism, not merely the fastest software?"

Transition

"The technical work also needs thresholds and a sequence that carries value."

Slide 16 - Consequence, threshold, and slice

Time: 6 minutes Job: Replace vague technical labels with decision-relevant product consequences.

Rehearse

"Reforge argues that the tech-debt label hides different work. Scale work creates future capacity or quality; risk work reduces the likelihood or consequence of operational, security, or regulatory incidents.S3-SN-09 Those outcomes create shared decision language."
"For Noted, the risk threshold is clear: do not pilot customer recordings until retention, deletion, and access controls pass review. The scale threshold says not to build a multi-region pipeline until concurrency or latency blocks the target workflow. The economic threshold revisits vendor versus owned inference when unit cost or margin crosses a named bound."
"The sequence starts with a manual workflow, moves to API-assisted shadow mode, then a two-partner bounded pilot, and only then operationalizes. Smaller is not automatically better. Each slice must still produce coherent value or decision evidence."

Misconception recovery

If a learner says the agent can build the whole capability in one week:

"That is a production estimate. What review, integration, security, data, support, and operational work remains—and who has capacity for it?"

Transition

"Now choose the option and follow its consequences."

Slide 17 - Unit 9 individual decision

Time: 14 minutes total: 6 decide, 8 debrief Job: Observe AI-era technical product judgment rather than tool fluency.

Set up the decision

"Choose build, buy, adapt, defer, or no-build for decision-handoff intelligence. State what coding agents materially change, what remains costly, where the scope-time-quality-ownership risk moves, the relevant threshold, smallest value-bearing sequence, specialist review, and operational owner."

Model debrief

"I choose no-build first, then stage an adapted model-API approach in shadow mode. Coding agents lower the effort to explore workflow logic, adapters, and evaluation tooling. They do not remove the need for representative evaluation, data handling, integration, failure recovery, monitoring, vendor economics, or an owner."
"I will not expose customer recordings until security and data-retention review passes. I start with manual handoff, move to shadow suggestions reviewed by the team, then a two-partner pilot. Engineering owns the runtime; product owns the value threshold; security and legal validate data consequence."
"The displaced risk is review and integration capacity. The team can create more options than it can responsibly understand and operate."

What strong judgment sounds like

  • The learner distinguishes code generation from product ownership.
  • The choice compares credible alternatives, including no-build and defer.
  • The lifecycle includes data, security, integration, reliability, economics, maintenance, and support where relevant.
  • A threshold authorizes or blocks the next commitment.
  • The specialist boundary and operational owner are named.

Weak-answer recovery

If the answer is "build because it is core":

"Which part is actually differentiating: the model output, the context system, the workflow, or the distribution? What evidence supports owning that layer?"

Transition

"We can now assemble the Week 3 record."

Slide 18 - Strategy and Constraint Choice

Time: 5 minutes Job: Integrate the three decisions into one portable capstone checkpoint.

Rehearse

"The record begins with diagnosis and direction: the situation, winning mechanism, linked hypotheses, weakest link, and exclusions."
"Then it makes the portfolio explicit: funded value types, displaced opportunity, capacity emphasis, owners, sequence, and revision points."
"Finally, it records the technical calculus: chosen option, rejected alternatives, lifecycle consequences, thresholds, specialist review, and operational owner."
"Check for contradiction. If the strategy claims workflow trust while the technical choice ignores data governance, the record is not coherent. If the portfolio funds horizontal expansion while the direction claims enterprise depth, the choice is not portable."

Capstone handoff

For the learner's own Product Decision Case, require the same four blocks. No prototype or code is required.

Transition

"Session 4 begins where a strategy presentation usually ends: other people must commit, adapt, and learn from what happens."

Slide 19 - Coherent commitment with visible conditions

Time: 9 minutes total: 3 synthesize, 6 Q&A Job: Close the strategy arc and set up organizational commitment without consensus.

Rehearse

"An opinionated choice is not a claim of certainty. It is a coherent commitment whose evidence, exclusions, conditions, and ownership are visible."
"Carry forward the chosen direction. Make the constraints and ownership portable. In Session 4, we will create commitment without requiring consensus, adapt execution without taking ownership back, and evaluate outcomes without rewriting the original logic."
"Bring the choice record, not a polished roadmap. The next question is whether the people who must act understand what is decided, where their judgment begins, and what evidence can reopen the call."

Open Q&A boundary

Welcome questions about strategy, portfolio, sequencing, technical trade-offs, thresholds, and ownership. Park questions about agent brands, prompt technique, repository setup, or code generation:

"That belongs in an optional Product Builder or book continuation. This course is testing Core PM judgment about whether and how the product should own the capability."

Final check

Ask learners to complete one sentence privately:

"Because we chose ___, we will fund ___, defer ___, and revisit when ___."

If any blank cannot be completed, the Week 3 choice is not yet portable.

Facilitator diagnostic appendix

Model choice record for Noted

FieldModel response
DiagnosisTrusted ownership handoff, not note creation, is the consequential constraint in recurring enterprise decision meetings.
DirectionDeepen the decision-handoff workflow for a narrow enterprise audience.
Winning mechanismMeeting context makes explicit decisions and owners trustworthy; admin templates distribute the workflow; team economics support governance and service cost.
ExclusionDefer general personal summarization, sales intelligence, and every-meeting expansion.
Weakest linkRepeatable admin-led distribution.
Revision triggerAdmin adoption stalls, governance prevents use, or handoff does not improve repeat behavior in the two-partner cycle.
PortfolioHandoff feature; minimum permissions and retention; admin distribution test; meeting-type instrumentation.
Displaced opportunityBroader self-serve reach and sales-use-case expansion.
SequenceManual distribution test; value-bearing handoff slice; minimum controls; evidence-based deepen-expand-stop decision.
Technical optionNo-build workflow first; then adapt a model API in shadow mode; defer an owned end-to-end model capability.
AI-era changeLower option-generation and prototype cost; higher relative importance of context, evaluation, review, integration, and lifecycle ownership.
ThresholdsNo customer recording pilot before data controls pass; no scale architecture before observed constraint; revisit vendor economics at a named unit-cost bound.
OwnersProduct owns value threshold; engineering owns runtime and integration; security/legal validate data consequence; a named platform owner carries operations.

Common failure modes and interventions

Failure modeWhat it sounds likeFacilitator intervention
Goal presented as strategy"Win two enterprise customers""What diagnosis and winning mechanism make that goal achievable?"
Framework completeness mistaken for coherence"We filled all six dimensions""Which links reinforce one another, and which one can break the system?"
No real exclusion"We can still do the other idea lightly""What capacity is displaced, and which direction governs the conflict?"
Single-signal fit"Retention looks good, so we have PMF""What do growth, advantage, economics, and the target segment say?"
Portfolio as equal buckets"Give every category 20 percent""Which mix fits the current strategy and stage?"
Score owns the call"RICE says 168""Which inputs are assumptions, and what strategic constraint is missing?"
Sequence as chronology"Do A, then B, then C""What dependency, evidence, or option does that order create?"
AI equals free engineering"The agent can build it this week""What remains to review, integrate, secure, release, support, and own?"
Build because unique"No vendor has our exact workflow""Is uniqueness a differentiator, or merely a customization need?"
Tech debt as self-justification"Engineering needs debt time""What consequence and threshold earn the capacity?"

Used only to establish that software development is a material agent use case and that agentic coding often involves automation.

  5. S3-SN-13

    METR, “Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity”, 2025. Randomized controlled study of 16 experienced maintainers completing 246 tasks in mature repositories. Used as a boundary against universal productivity claims, not as a universal slowdown claim.

  6. S3-SN-01

    Reforge, Mastering Product Management, “Creating Strategic Foundations,” and Product Strategy, “Great Product Strategy.” Durable course use: product strategy explains how the product will win; local work should reinforce the deeper mechanism rather than only surface goals.

  7. S3-SN-03

    Reforge, Finding Product-Market Fit, “Measuring PMF Deliberately,” “Measuring and Evaluating Growth,” “Retention,” and “Engagement.” Durable course use: no single metric should be treated as sufficient proof of product-market fit.

  8. S3-SN-09

    Reforge, Technical Strategy, “The Limitations of Tech Debt,” “Scale Work Outcomes and Thresholds,” and “Risk Work Outcomes and Thresholds.” Durable course use: replace the ambiguous debt label with explicit capacity, quality, reliability, risk, and strategic consequences.

  9. S3-SN-06

    Reforge, Product Strategy, “Identifying Strategic Priorities.” Durable course use: product leaders translate relevant company priorities into product-area choices rather than repeating top-down language.

  10. S3-SN-04

    Reforge, Mastering Product Management, “Introduction: The Problem with RICE,” “The 4 Lenses,” and “Prioritizing Objectives and Initiatives.” Durable course use: broaden candidate value and use quantitative inputs to support, not replace, accountable prioritization.

  11. S3-SN-07

    Reforge, Product Strategy, “Developing a Product Workplan.” Durable course use: a workplan sequences product work over multiple periods and protects longer-term value from short-term roadmap pressure.

  12. S3-SN-11

    Reforge, Technical Strategy, “Scope, Time, and Resource Trade-Offs” and “Break Up Problems and Sequence Work.” Durable course use: constraints remain coupled, and smaller sequences should deliver coherent value while preserving the long-term portfolio.

  13. S3-SN-10

    Reforge, Technical Strategy, “Build or Buy Trade-Offs.” Durable course use: compare strategic value, available resources, cost, and vendor reliability; unique does not automatically mean differentiating.
